title: A cell-sorting-based protocol for cell cycle small-scale ChIP sequencing
protocol: Seed 2.5 × 10^6 RPE cells in four 15 cm² plates for 48 hours.
Incubate the seeded cells with Hoechst 33342, adding 1/1000 directly to the medium and incubating at 37°C for 1 hour.
Shake off loosely attached mitotic cells by tapping the sides of the plates.
Collect the medium in a 50 mL conical tube and centrifuge to pellet less adherent mitotic cells.
Transfer the spun medium into another tube, leaving enough behind to avoid aspirating pelleted cells.
Rinse the cells with 1× PBS.
Add 2.5 ml of trypsin per 15 cm² plate for a single cell suspension critical for sorting.
Resuspend the cells in 36 mL of medium for four 15 cm² plates.
Transfer the resuspended cells into a 50 mL conical tube containing the pellet of mitotic cells.
Add 1 mL of 37% formaldehyde to the medium (final concentration of 1%).
Incubate at 37°C for 13 minutes.
Add 3.7 mL of glycine 1.25 M pH 2.5 to stop fixation (0.125 M final concentration).
Incubate for at least 2 minutes at 18°C–25°C.
Centrifuge the cells and wash the cell pellet with 1× PBS.
Centrifuge again after washing.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 2 mL of spun medium from step 3.
Place the resuspended cells on ice until sorting.
Sort the cells using a BD FACS Fusion with the BV421-A laser.
Transfer cells to 15 mL conical tubes and centrifuge for 15 min at 1,000 g at 4°C.
Lyse the cells in 200 μL cellular lysis buffer complemented with fresh proteinase inhibitors (cocktail tablets EDTA free), incubate for 5 min on ice.
Centrifuge the lysed cells for 5 min at 2,000 g at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in nuclear lysis buffer complemented with fresh proteinase inhibitors (adjust volume based on number of cells).
Sonicate the chromatin as needed.
Turn on the QSonica Q800R chiller.
Transfer collected chromatin into 0.5 mL thin wall PCR tubes.
Sonicate according to the time determined in the optimization step.
Add 3 μL of chromatin and 1 μL of proteinase K to 65 μL of elution buffer.
Incubate at 65°C for 4–16 hours in a benchtop thermomixer shaking at 1,000 rpm.
Add 65 μL of phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol 25:24:1 to the mixture.
Vortex the mixture thoroughly.
Centrifuge the mixture for 1 minute at full speed at 18°C–25°C.
Take 20 μL of the upper phase from the centrifuged mixture.
Mix the taken portion with appropriate dye.
Run the mixed sample on a 1% agarose gel.
Check if the chromatin is under 300 bp.
Transfer the sonicated chromatin to 1.5 mL tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes for 10 min at 20,000 g at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to clean tubes, leaving any potential pellet behind.
Leave the chromatin at 18°C–25°C for a few minutes before proceeding with further steps.
Store the chromatin at -80°C until ready for use.
Prebind the beads with the antibody.
In a 200 μL tube, add 100 μL dilution IP buffer complemented with fresh protease inhibitors (cocktail tablets EDTA free).
Add 2.5 μL protein A or G magnetic beads (prewashed and resuspended in dilution IP buffer) to the tube.
Add 0.2 μg of antibody to the tube.
Incubate at 4°C for 6 h under rotation.
Pool the chromatin in a 1.5 mL tube.
Include 0.5 μg of chromatin in 10 μL of nuclear lysis buffer with fresh protease inhibitors added (cocktail tablets EDTA free) per IP.
Include 0.5 μg of chromatin for input if using this to generate baseline input sequencing profiles.
Include 0.5 μg of chromatin for pipetting error.
Take 10 μL of the pooled chromatin diluted in nuclear lysis buffer.
Store the input sample at 4°C until further use.
Bring the remaining pooled chromatin to a volume of 100 μL per IP with dilution IP buffer containing fresh protease inhibitors.
Add 2.5 μL of protein A agarose beads per IP, prewashed and resuspended in dilution IP buffer.
Incubate at 4°C for 2 h under rotation.
Centrifuge to separate the chromatin from the beads.
Transfer the supernatant containing the chromatin into another tube.
Add 2.5 μL of protein A (or G) magnetic beads per IP, prewashed and resuspended in dilution IP buffer.
Incubate at 4°C for 2 h under rotation.
Spin down tubes with beads/antibodies and place them on a magnetic rack before removing the supernatant.
Add 100 μL of precleared chromatin per tube, incubate at 4°C for 12–16 hours with rotation.
Place the tubes on a magnet after spinning to remove the supernatant.
Wash the beads twice with dilution IP buffer.
Wash the beads once with TSE buffer.
Wash the beads once with LiCl buffer.
Wash the beads twice with TE buffer.
Add 50 μL of elution buffer to the beads and transfer in a 1.5 mL tube.
Add 1 μL of RNAseA 100 μg/μL and incubate at 37°C for 30 min in a benchtop thermomixer shaking at 1,000 rpm.
Add 1 μL of proteinase K (10 mg/mL) and incubate at 37°C for 1 hour in a benchtop thermomixer shaking at 1,000 rpm.
Remove samples from beads and incubate at 65°C for 4 hours shaking at 1,000 rpm.
Add 125 μL of Agencourt AMPure XP to both de-crosslinked IPs and input, then incubate for 10 minutes at 18-25°C.
Place tubes on magnet and remove supernatant.
Add 450 μL of freshly prepared 70% EtOH, place tubes on magnet, and remove supernatant again.
Repeat the ethanol wash once more.
Wait for beads to dry under light observation; do not over-dry.
Resuspend dried beads in 40 μL of H2O and incubate for 1 minute at 18-25°C.
Place tubes on magnet and remove liquid from beads, leaving them ready for DNA purification or storage.
Work on a clean bench with clean pipetmans and sterile filter tips to avoid exogenous DNA contamination.
Quantify each ChIP DNA using a Qubit dsDNA HS Assay Kit.
Place each DNA in a well of a 96 well plate, bringing the volume up to 50 μL with H2O.
Perform end repair as directed on page 11 of the Illumina PDF.
Adenylate 3′ ends as directed on page 14 of the Illumina PDF.
Ligate adapters.
Enrich DNA fragments.
Add 30 μL of AMPure beads to the 50 μL PCR reaction.
Incubate at 18°C–25°C for 10 min.
Place the tubes on the magnetic stand.
Transfer 77 μL of the sample in new wells.
Discard the beads.
Add 12 μL of AMPure beads.
Incubate at 18°C–25°C for 10 min.
Place the plate on the magnetic stand.
Take off 80 μL of the sample and discard.
Perform two washes with 200 μL of fresh prepped 80% EtOH.
Dry the beads.
Resuspend the beads in 17.5 μL of resuspension buffer.
Incubate at 18°C–25°C for 1 min.
Place the plate on the magnetic stand.
Transfer 15 μL of each library in the final plate.
Validate the libraries using a TapeStation or a Bioanalyzer.
Proceed to sequencing.
